analysis.title: CIO View: High yield
key_insights: UBS CIO holds an Attractive absolute view on high yield and a Preferred relative view versus other fixed income segments. US and EUR HY yields are 8.6% and 6.9%.

US and EUR HY spreads are nearly 100bps wider than the summer lows, at about 340bps for both. The widening is concentrated in lower-rated credits, with CCC spreads above 1,000bps. It is not a broad risk-off move.

UBS expects high-single-digit total returns over the next 12 months, driven mostly by carry and duration with some spread compression. It argues the market overestimates the path for policy rates and that current spreads price more default risk than UBS estimates.
Performance was weakest among AI-related issuers and a few distressed media and communications companies. Pure-play neocloud bonds sold off sharply, with yields on select companies above 16%.

AI earnings season is nearly over and most AI companies met expectations. Commentary gave little sign of an imminent capex pause despite higher financing costs. AI-linked data center issuers are only about 3% of the US HY market.

The US midterms gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress. UBS assumes this raises the chance of more AI regulation and a pause in construction of some AI data centers in certain states. UBS says it is early days.

The key question is how far AI companies keep relying on debt financing. Less bond supply from improved balance sheets would support credit. Less financing because of falling confidence in the underlying cash flows would raise downside risk.
Default activity is low at 1.8% in US HY and 1.3% in Euro HY at end-September (trailing 12-month, par-weighted). UBS expects about 2% in both regions over the next 12 months.
US HY leverage is about 4.3x and interest coverage about 4.3x, per Bank of America data. Refinancing was about 63% of US HY issuance last year and over 50% this year, and CCC issuance is subdued.

The distress ratio rose to 7.5% in US HY and 7.0% in EUR HY at end-October, skewed by CCC issuers. The issuer-weighted increase is much smaller. BB bonds are about 60% of the US index and CCC 8%, and secured bonds are a record of about a third.

In EUR HY, BBs are about 70% of the market and CCC about 4%. US ratings actions have skewed toward upgrades over the last three months. Some distressed issuers are pursuing liability management exercises rather than hard defaults, which may mean higher recoveries.

UBS expects index-level defaults to stay low but spread dispersion to rise within lower-rated segments, and recommends an active and selective approach. About USD 201bn, or 10% of the US HY market, matures by end-2028, which UBS calls manageable. The hardest refinancing is concentrated in CCC bonds.
UBS says spreads have overshot its target levels. Its Dec 2027 targets in the base case are 300bps for both US and EUR HY, against current spreads of 347bps for US and 339bps for EUR.

sector_views.rationale: UBS rates the asset class Attractive and Preferred on elevated yields, low duration, low default expectations and solid fundamentals.
AI-related issuers and pure-play neoclouds lagged on funding costs and capex concerns, with yields on select names above 16%. UBS calls for selectivity.
CCC spreads are above 1,000bps and dispersion is expected to rise in lower-rated segments. UBS recommends an active and selective approach.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight high yield credit (US and EUR) as an asset class, with an active and selective approach within lower-rated segments
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated yields, low duration, low default expectations and spreads that overshoot UBS targets support high-single-digit 12-month total returns.
trade_ideas.risk: AI funding and capex concerns, higher rates, and rising dispersion in CCC and lower-rated credits.

risk_factors: Higher rates or sticky inflation could weigh on lower-rated issuers with limited debt-servicing capacity.
AI capex and funding concerns, plus possible AI regulation and data center construction pauses after the US midterms.
Declining confidence in the cash flows behind AI-related debt could deepen the downside in credit.
Prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption or damage to energy infrastructure would push oil, inflation and longer-term yields up.
In the AI bear market scenario, US HY spreads reach 650bps and Euro HY 630bps by Dec 2027.
Rising spread dispersion in lower-rated segments and a CCC refinancing wall, with USD 201bn (10% of the US market) maturing by end-2028.
charts_described: The spread table shows ICE BofA US HY at 347bps and Euro HY at 339bps on 18 Nov 2026, with UBS targets of 300bps for both in Jun 2027 and Dec 2027.
vol_and_positioning: CCC spreads have widened to more than 1,000bps, and yields on select pure-play neocloud bonds are above 16%.
The US HY distress ratio is 7.5% and the EUR ratio 7.0%, both skewed by CCC issuers.
Secured bonds are a record of about a third of US HY outstanding, and BBs are about 60% of the US index.
geopolitical: Conflict in the Middle East: the upside scenario assumes a swift resolution that stabilizes oil below USD 90/bbl.
Prolonged disruption of flows through the Strait of Hormuz or destruction of energy infrastructure would keep oil prices under upward pressure in the downside scenario.
US midterm elections gave Democrats control of both houses of Congress, which UBS expects to bring more AI regulation and possible pauses in some data center construction.

tension_points.bull_case: Widening is concentrated in a handful of CCC credits. Fundamentals are intact, with default rates of 1.8% US and 1.3% EUR, leverage of 4.3x, and a base-case total return in the high single digits. UBS sees spreads overshooting its targets.
tension_points.bear_case: AI funding and capex concerns, a rising distress ratio of 7.5% in the US, and rising dispersion in lower-rated credits. In the AI bear market scenario, US HY spreads reach 650bps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker AI financing driven by declining confidence in the cash flows behind the debt, which UBS says would deteriorate the credit outlook.

theme_stances.key_argument: Elevated yields, low defaults and sound fundamentals support high-single-digit total returns.
theme_stances.evidence: We hold an Attractive view on high yield (HY).
